scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by making that Facebook post about my best friend's trip to India. Let me start by going through the situation again to make sure I understand everything. My best friend, who's 21, went on a three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive! Plus, he paid for the entire trip himself, which cost over $3000. That's a lot of money, so I can imagine he must have saved up for a while or maybe took out some loans. Now, he's a pretty shy and quiet guy. I know he doesn't like to talk about himself a lot, especially when it comes to his achievements or things he's done that are out of the ordinary. Before he left, he didn't tell many people about the trip, and I'm not sure he would have told anyone when he got back if I hadn't done something about it. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he was doing. I mean, he did something really selfless and important, and I wanted people to know about it. So, I decided to make a Facebook post about him to let all his friends and family know what he had done. I did this while he was away, about a week before he was going to come home. Because of where he was in India, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I couldn't wait to see him and went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but he said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn't want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he's such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post, and I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, was I AITA (Ask If It's Too Awkward) for making that post? Alright, so now I need to figure out whether I did the right thing or not. Let's break this down step by step. First, I need to consider my friend's personality. He's shy and quiet, and he didn't tell many people about the trip before he left. That suggests that he's not someone who likes to draw attention to himself. He went on this trip for self-improvement, not necessarily to help others, although he did do volunteer work. But he felt that his main reason was self-improvement, and he didn't want people to think he was bragging or trying to be seen as a great person. I made the Facebook post to give him recognition for his work, thinking that he wouldn't do it himself because he's shy. But he ended up being upset about it. So, was it wrong of me to do that? I think it's important to consider the following points: 1. **Respect for Privacy**: My friend didn't tell many people about his trip, which indicates that he might not have wanted it to be widely known. By posting about it on Facebook, I might have violated his privacy. 2. **Intentions vs. Impact**: My intention was to give him recognition and celebrate his achievements. However, the impact was that he felt uncomfortable and upset because he didn't want attention for his actions. 3. **Communication**: I didn't ask him before posting about him. If I had communicated with him about my intention to post, he could have expressed his feelings beforehand, and we could have avoided the conflict. 4. **Understanding His Needs**: Since he's shy and prefers not to draw attention to himself, I should have considered his needs and preferences before taking action that could affect him. 5. **Consequences of the Post**: The post was positive, but it still brought unwanted attention to him. He felt that it misrepresented his reasons for going on the trip and made him uncomfortable. 6. **His Reaction**: He was clearly upset about the post, which shows that it had a negative impact on him despite my good intentions. 7. **My Feelings**: I felt that I was doing something nice, but I didn't consider his perspective. It's important to balance my desire to celebrate him with his need for privacy and lack of desire for attention. 8. **Future Actions**: Moving forward, it's important to communicate with him before sharing personal or sensitive information about him. This can help prevent similar conflicts in the future. So, considering all these points, it seems like making the Facebook post without his consent was not the right thing to do. Even though my intentions were good, I didn't respect his privacy and his preference for not drawing attention to himself. By not communicating with him beforehand, I took an action that had a negative impact on our relationship. It's important to prioritize his feelings and preferences, especially since he's someone who values privacy and doesn't like attention. In the future, I should make sure to talk to him before sharing such personal information about him to ensure that I'm respecting his boundaries and that we're both comfortable with the situation. Additionally, it's a good lesson in understanding that what I perceive as a kind gesture might not always be what the other person wants or needs. Taking the time to communicate and understand each other's perspectives can help prevent misunderstandings and conflicts. In conclusion, while my intention was to celebrate my friend's achievements, making the Facebook post without his consent was not the right thing to do. It's important to respect his privacy, communicate with him before sharing personal information, and consider his feelings and preferences in the future.
